title: Observability: ECDSA pool exhaustion returns WC_HW_E with no diagnostic log
description:
crypto2dev_ecdsa() acquires a pool slot for sign and verify operations (lines ~1480, ~1550). If the pool is exhausted (op_fd < 0), the code sets ret=WC_HW_E and jumps to the cleanup label with no WOLFSSL_MSG. The cipher, hash, and HMAC paths all emit 'pool exhausted — increase WOLFSSL_CRYPTO2DEV_POOL_SIZE' before returning WC_HW_E; the ECDSA paths do not.

Trigger: all pool slots are in use when wc_EccSign or wc_EccVerify is called under the crypto2dev devId (e.g. TLS handshake with many concurrent connections and an undersized pool).

Bad outcome: the caller gets WC_HW_E with no context. A support engineer debugging 'TLS handshake fails with WC_HW_E during ECDSA sign' has no indication that the pool is the problem rather than the hardware. The fix is the same two-line pattern used for cipher/hash/HMAC: check g_pool.slots != NULL after acquire fails and emit the 'pool exhausted' message.
